full_judgment:
11. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that although a major penalty in the form of compulsory retirement has been imposed upon the petitioner, mandatory provision of rule 143 sub-rule 2 of Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 has been grossly violated and the petitioner was not afforded an opportunity of filing written defence as provided by sub-rule 2 of rule 143 and thus he has been seriously prejudiced and the entire proceeding was vitiated for such violation of the Rule. 

 14. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos.1 to 3, however, submits that the authority held due inquiry and after complying with the provisions laid down in rule 143 of the Power Development Board Employees Service Rules, 1982 the authority was satisfied that the petitioner was guilty of negligence to his duty and imposed the penalty as evidence by Annexure I-(1) which is legal and proper. The petitioner did not exhaust the remedy available to him under the Power Development Board Service Rules, 1982 and, as such, this Rule is not maintainable. 

 16. Sub-rules 1, 2 and 3 of rule 143 of Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 run as follows: 

 17. From a reading of rule 143 it appears that the petitioner is entitled to get another show cause notice by the authority to submit written defence to them but on perusal of Annexure ''F'' the charge sheet it appears that instead of complying with sub-rule 2 the authority directed the petitioner to submit his reply to one Tapan Kumar Das, the inquiry officer, under sub-rule 3 of rule 143 and, as such, the authority neither called for any written defence nor considered the same, rather directed the petitioner to submit his reply to the inquiry officer which, in our opinion, has seriously prejudiced the petitioner in defending himself in the proceeding and it is a gross violation of sub-rule (2) rule 143 of the PDB (Employees) Service Rules. 

 20. In the facts and circumstances of the case we do not find justification in imposing major penalty upon the petitioner as has been done by the impugned Annexure 41) and there has been gross violation of sub-rule 2 of rule 143 of the Bangladesh. Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared as having been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
